themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 28 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 4.2 per week over 8 weeks (559% increase, z-score 13.3), suggesting either a sudden infrastructure failure event or a new wave of pothole/pavement damage in Central Harlem.
evidence: 28 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.2 weekly baseline (z-score: 13.3)
Statistically significant spike indicates acute rather than chronic problem
Aligns with long-standing CB budget request for DEP capital improvements, suggesting systemic underinvestment
reporting_angles: Canvas specific blocks/neighborhoods to map where complaints cluster and identify common trigger (weather event, construction, deferred maintenance)
Interview residents about impact on daily commuting, biking, accessibility for elderly/disabled residents

themes_detail.label: Massive Tree Damage Spike
themes_detail.summary: Damaged tree complaints hit 5 THIS WEEK compared to a baseline of 0.1 per week over 8 weeks (3900% surge, z-score 14.74), the highest statistical anomaly in the dataset, suggesting acute storm damage, disease outbreak, or landscaping emergency in a specific area.
evidence: 5 damaged tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (3900% increase, z-score: 14.74)
Highest z-score spike across entire complaint dataset
Timing suggests weather event (high winds/storm) or sudden infestation/disease
reporting_angles: Identify whether complaints cluster on specific blocks or throughout district; check Parks Dept storm damage assessments
Interview Parks Dept about emergency tree removal protocol and timeline for affected neighborhoods

themes_detail.label: Street Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped to 160 LAST WEEK versus a baseline of 39.2 per week (308% increase, z-score 11.01), nearly quadrupling typical complaints and suggesting a new source of disruption (construction, street vendor activity, events, or ongoing nightlife disturbance).
evidence: 160 street/sidewalk noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 39.2 weekly baseline (308% increase, z-score: 11.01)
Vendor enforcement complaints also spiked 1500% LAST WEEK (4 vs. 0.2 baseline), suggesting possible correlation with street vending activity
Street sweeping complaints up 454% LAST WEEK (9 vs. 1.6 baseline), indicating possible sanitation/street activity
reporting_angles: Identify specific blocks/neighborhoods with clustering and determine if tied to single event (street fair, concert, new venue) or distributed enforcement crackdown on vendors
Interview residents about noise sources (construction hours? outdoor dining expansion? new nightlife venues?) and NYPD/311 response

themes_detail.label: Sanitation System Strain
themes_detail.summary: Sanitation-related complaints show a coordinated spike LAST WEEK: street sweeping up 454% (9 vs. 1.6 baseline), sanitation worker complaints up 700% 2 WEEKS AGO (3 vs. 0.4 baseline), and commercial disposal up 1100% 2 WEEKS AGO (3 vs. 0.2 baseline), suggesting either workforce shortage, service gaps, or contamination/cleanliness crisis.
evidence: Street sweeping complaints: 9 LAST WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly baseline (454% increase, z-score: 5.6)
Sanitation worker/vehicle complaints: 3 at 2-WEEK mark vs. 0.4 baseline (700% increase, z-score: 5.42)
Commercial disposal: 3 at 2-WEEK mark vs. 0.2 baseline (1100% increase, z-score: 6.35)
Unsanitary condition remains high volume complaint (1,257 over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Sanitation for explanation of coverage gaps or staffing changes in CD110 over past 2 weeks
Interview residents and business owners about visible trash accumulation and response time on specific blocks

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk/Root Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Root, sewer, and sidewalk condition complaints spiked to 4 complaints 3 WEEKS AGO versus a baseline of 0.6 per week (540% increase, z-score 4.85), suggesting either unseasonable root growth, aging infrastructure failure, or flooding damage that preceded recent street condition spike.
evidence: 4 root/sewer/sidewalk complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.6 weekly baseline (540% increase, z-score: 4.85)
Timing precedes this week's street condition surge, suggesting cascade of infrastructure failures
Door/window complaints elevated at 686 over 90 days, may indicate structural stress from root damage
reporting_angles: Map root damage complaints against tree species, age of sidewalk infrastructure, and DEP sewer maintenance records
Interview DEP about assessment of aging sewer/sidewalk system in Central Harlem and emergency repair capacity
